title: Bidirectional A* in Reykjavík: Meet in the Middle!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* slice through Reykjavík’s street graph by expanding paths from both start and goal at once. The two frontiers use consistent heuristics to meet efficiently, producing a fast shortest-route visualization on a real-world map.
ig_caption:
🌍🗺️ Reykjavík (Miðborg) street grid, but make it computational⚡

In this reel, we run **Bidirectional A***: instead of searching from only the start, we build two A* searches—one forward from the source and one backward from the destination—until their frontiers “meet.” 🤝

🧠 **How it works (graph theory mode):**
Your city streets become a weighted **graph** (intersections = nodes, road segments = edges). Each A* expansion prioritizes nodes by
**f(n) = g(n) + h(n)**, where **g(n)** is the known cost so far and **h(n)** is a heuristic estimate to the target. With **Bidirectional A***, you effectively reduce the explored area because both sides shrink the remaining search space—like two teams solving the same maze from opposite ends. 🧩

📍On real street maps, this often means fewer expansions than unidirectional search while still landing on an optimal (or consistent-heuristic-guaranteed) route. ✅
